tools.name: call_flowie_api

Authentication, the organization header and the audit trail are added automatically, and an 'organization_id'/'organizationId' path or query argument is filled in from the current organization: never pass tokens or action-performed-by headers, and leave the organization id out unless you deliberately target a different organization.

headers.description: Extra request headers, for headers the operation does not list. Use for cross-cutting ones: 'Request-Id' to tag a call for tracing, 'skip-flows'/'skip-notifications' (with their -reason companions) to suppress downstream automation, 'Idempotency-Key' to make a retry safe. tools.name: create_transaction_document
tools.title: Create transaction document
tools.description: Create one transaction document (invoice, credit note, debit note, purchase order, sales order, quote…) in the Flowie app, as the acting organization. Minimal call: `documentType`, `number`, `issuedAt`, the other party (`buyerId` when you sell, `sellerId` when you buy — the acting organization is the other side) and `lineItems`, each with `description`, `quantity`, `unitPrice` (excl. tax) and `taxRate` (a percentage: 20 for 20 %). Every amount is computed from the lines — net, VAT and gross per line and for the document — so pass `totalAmountExclTax` / `totalAmountInclTax` only to override them, or when there are no lines. Returns the document with its `id`. Posting the same type, number, seller and year twice returns the existing document instead of a duplicate; `idempotency_key` makes a retry of the exact same call safe. One document per call: to create documents in bulk, from a system, or to send e-invoices over Peppol, use the Exchange API (`POST /exchange/v1/documents/send`) or its MCP server at /exchange/mcp.

documentType.description: What the document is. INVOICE, CREDIT_NOTE and DEBIT_NOTE are the e-invoicing ones.

number.description: The document number as printed on it (invoice number, BT-1).

sellerId.description: Organization id of the seller (the supplier, who is owed the money). Omit when the acting organization sells; then name the buyer in `buyerId`.

buyerId.description: Organization id of the buyer (the customer, who pays). Omit when the acting organization buys; then name the seller in `sellerId`. Find an id with list_partnerships or search_organizations.

lineItems.description: The lines. `priceWithoutTax`, `tax` and `priceWithTax` are computed (quantity × unitPrice, less `discountRate` %, then `taxRate` %) unless you state them. Any other field of a transaction-documents line (unitOfMeasure, supplierItemId, buyerItemId, vatCategoryCode, deliveryDueDate…) passes through as is.

unitPrice.description: Price of one unit, excluding tax.

taxRate.description: VAT rate as a percentage: 20 for 20 %, 5.5 for 5.5 %, 1 for 1 %. A value between 0 and 1 (0.2) is refused as ambiguous. Default 0.

discountRate.description: Line discount as a percentage (10 for 10 %); a value between 0 and 1 is refused as ambiguous.

unitOfMeasure.description: PIECE, HOUR, DAY, KILOGRAM, LITRE, METRE… Default PIECE on the platform.

priceWithoutTax.description: Line net amount. Computed when omitted.

tax.description: Line VAT amount. Computed when omitted.

priceWithTax.description: Line gross amount. Computed when omitted.

totalAmountExclTax.description: Document net total. Computed from the lines when omitted; required without lines.

totalAmountInclTax.description: Document total including VAT (BT-112). Computed from the lines when omitted; required without lines.

notes.description: Free text shown on the document.

purchaseOrderId.description: Number of the purchase order this document settles (BT-13).

salesOrderReference.description: Number of the seller's sales order this document refers to (BT-14).

originalInvoiceId.description: For a credit or debit note: the number of the invoice it corrects (BT-25).

paymentInstructions.description: How to pay, as free text (payment terms, IBAN reference…).

prepaymentRequired.description: Whether payment is due before delivery. Default false.

idempotency_key.description: Any opaque string (≤ 255 chars): a retry carrying the same key returns the first result instead of creating twice.

additional_fields.description: Any other field of POST /transaction-documents/v4/documents, passed as is and winning over the computed body: documentSubtype, allowanceCharges, recipientEmails, buyerReference, contractReference, invoicingPeriodStart/End, paymentTermsId, parties (a full party list replaces the two built here)…

tools.title: Get document audit log
tools.description: Get the full change history / audit trail of a transaction document (invoice, credit note, debit note, purchase order, purchase request): who did what, and when. Returns one entry per recorded action, each with createdAt, actionBy, actorType, actorId and changeDetails. STATUS CHANGES, INCLUDING APPROVALS AND REFUSALS, ARE NOT THEIR OWN ACTION: they appear as a `party_updated` entry whose changeDetails holds the field-level JSON-patch, e.g. {op: replace, path: /lifecycleStatus, old: received, value: refused}. To find who approved or refused a document and when, read changeDetails for /lifecycleStatus — do not expect an action literally named approved or rejected. Observed actions: created, updated, viewed, party_created, party_updated, party_deleted, line_item_created, line_item_updated, bulk_line_status_updated. When actorType is null the actor is UNKNOWN — report it as unknown, and do not attribute the change to a flow run, an integration or any automation. actorType is USER, FLOW_RUN or INTEGRATION only when explicitly set, and actorId then identifies that actor (e.g. the flow run id). Use this to answer 'who rejected this invoice and when', 'when was it created', 'who changed this purchase order', 'what changed it and why is it in this status'.

Search the files of the organization's Documents menu (the document store, called 'Documents' in the Flowie app): every file the org holds, uploaded by a user or received from an integration, e.g. the D365 business events stored as 'event-<id>.json'. This is NOT the Exchange inbox and NOT invoices/orders (transaction documents). Use it to find or COUNT files received in a period: pass created_after/created_before with a time (ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-11-19T11:24:00+01:00) and read 'total_documents' in the result (exact; no need to page). Returns file name, type, size, dates and associated objects.

To filter or count by what is INSIDE the files (a field of a JSON or XML file, e.g. a business event's BusinessEventId, or any text), add content_match / content_contains / count_by together with a date window: the tool then reads every file of the window and returns matched_count, counts per value of count_by, and complete (true only when every file was read; if false, say so and give incomplete_because).

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the file name or description, plus a full-text match on the file's metadata (e.g. 'event-'). To count by date only, leave it empty. It does not search file content: use content_match / content_contains for that.

content_match.description: Keep only files whose content has these field values, e.g. {"BusinessEventId": "PMURFEP2PSelfbillingBusinessEvent"}. JSON: key path with dots for nesting (a bare key also matches at any depth). XML: element name at any depth. Case-insensitive exact value; "*" = field present. Needs a date window.

content_contains.description: Keep only files whose raw text contains this (case-insensitive). Needs a date window.

count_by.description: Field (same syntax as content_match) to break the matching files down by, e.g. 'BusinessEventId'. Returns 'counts'. Needs a date window.

max_documents.description: Content filters only: most files to read (default 20000, max 50000).

created_after.description: Only files created (received) at or after this instant (inclusive). ISO 8601, always with the offset: Europe/Paris is +01:00 in winter, +02:00 in summer.

created_before.description: Only files created (received) at or before this instant (inclusive). ISO 8601 with offset.

updated_after.description: Only files updated at or after this instant (inclusive). ISO 8601 with offset.

updated_before.description: Only files updated at or before this instant (inclusive). ISO 8601 with offset.

tools.name: save_report
tools.title: Save report
tools.description: Persist a new dashboard the user can reopen and refresh. Provide the data recipe (the Flowie read-tool calls that produce the data) and the HTML layout. It is saved as a DRAFT only the user (and whoever may edit it) sees; pass status=PUBLISHED only when the user asked to share or publish it. The `html` must be BODY-LEVEL content only (no // tags — the server wraps it in a sandboxed document with a strict CSP). It reads ALL data at render time from the global `window.REPORT_DATA`, an object keyed by each step's `key` (the value is that tool call's JSON result). NEVER hardcode data values. Do any aggregation (sums, group-by, top-N) in inline JS. Charts use Apache ECharts (the `echarts` global — already provided; do NOT add

steps.description:
Ordered data recipe. Each step replays one org-scoped Flowie READ tool (e.g. get_global_budget_metrics, search_purchase_orders, search_transaction_documents, list_partnerships, get_task_metrics). Results are org-scoped automatically. Only read-only tools are allowed (refresh must be side-effect-free).

COVER THE DATA. A search tool returns at most `limit` rows (100 max) and reports the size of the whole set in `total`. One step is therefore ONE PAGE: charting it while printing `total` as a KPI produces a dashboard that looks authoritative and is wrong. When `total` exceeds what one page returns, set `paginate: true` on the step: every replay then reads all pages of that ONE query and returns the rows merged under the same key (`documents`, `items`, …), so the report keeps up as the data grows. Do not write one step per offset. Otherwise narrow the query with filters or a date range, or state the covered range on the page. Prefer a server-side aggregate (get_global_budget_metrics, get_task_metrics) over paging thousands of rows.

key.description: Name this step's data under window.REPORT_DATA[key]

args.description: Arguments for the tool (no org id — injected automatically)

paginate.description: Read every page of this query on each replay (offset/limit until `total`, max 20,000 rows) and merge the rows under the same key.

steps.description:
Ordered data recipe. Each step replays one org-scoped Flowie READ tool (e.g. get_global_budget_metrics, search_purchase_orders, search_transaction_documents, list_partnerships, get_task_metrics). Results are org-scoped automatically. Only read-only tools are allowed (refresh must be side-effect-free).

COVER THE DATA. A search tool returns at most `limit` rows (100 max) and reports the size of the whole set in `total`. One step is therefore ONE PAGE: charting it while printing `total` as a KPI produces a dashboard that looks authoritative and is wrong. When `total` exceeds what one page returns, set `paginate: true` on the step: every replay then reads all pages of that ONE query and returns the rows merged under the same key (`documents`, `items`, …), so the report keeps up as the data grows. Do not write one step per offset. Otherwise narrow the query with filters or a date range, or state the covered range on the page. Prefer a server-side aggregate (get_global_budget_metrics, get_task_metrics) over paging thousands of rows.

# Flow rules (validator-enforced)
- Exactly ONE trigger node (first node, `type: EntityTriggerNode`).
- Every node has a unique `slug` within the flow.
- No cycles — a node cannot route back to a previous node.
- Terminal nodes use `nextNode: null` (or `nextIfTrue: null`, etc.).
- Required string fields are strings (use `""` when empty), NEVER null; omit optional fields rather than sending null. A null where the schema wants a string is stored but fails later in the editor at publish with `expected string, received null` (e.g. BranchNode `default` and every `branches[].name`). Routing slots like `nextNode`/`nextIfTrue` are the exception — they are legitimately `null` at terminals.

# Trigger nodes

`EntityTriggerNode` — flow starts when an entity is created/updated. The `entity` field is a NESTED object, not a string:
```json
{
  "type": "EntityTriggerNode",
  "slug": "trigger",
  "name": "On Invoice Created",
  "entity": {
    "type": "Invoice",
    "startMode": { "type": "OnEntityCreated" },
    "restartMode": { "type": "Manual" },
    "currencyConversion": { "type": "Disabled" },
    "includeVersionEvents": false
  },
  "filter": null,
  "nextNode": "next_step"
}
```
Entity types: `Invoice`, `CreditNote`, `DebitNote`, `PurchaseOrder`, `PurchaseRequest`, `Partnership`, `FormSubmission`, `Task`, `InboxEmail`, `As2Message`, `PaymentMethodInformation`.
`startMode.type`: `OnEntityCreated`, `OnEntityCreatedOrUpdated`, `Manual`. (`OnEntityUpdated` does NOT exist as a START mode — server rejects it.)
`restartMode.type`: `Manual` (one run per entity, ignores re-fires), `OnEntityUpdated`, or `OnEntityUpdatedIfSuspended`. (`Automatic` does NOT exist — server rejects it.)
The `entity` object has REQUIRED fields beyond `type`/`startMode`/`restartMode` that aren't always obvious — emit them all: `currencyConversion` (use `{ "type": "Disabled" }` unless converting to a target currency) and `includeVersionEvents` (use `false`). Omitting any returns 400 "Missing required field at 'nodes[0].entity.<field>'". (`create_flow` also defaults these server-side when absent, but emit them explicitly.)

`EntityTriggerNode` is the only trigger type to use for new flows. (The legacy `EventTriggerNodeV2` is deprecated — model any "on event X" brief as an `EntityTriggerNode` on the corresponding entity, e.g. an inbound-email flow triggers on `{type: "InboxEmail", startMode: {type: "OnEntityCreated"}}`.)

# Trigger filter shape (NOT a string)
`filter` is an object with nested `conditions` arrays — outer = OR, inner = AND:
```json
"filter": {
  "conditions": [
    [ "cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.lifecycleStatus == 'ON_HOLD'" ],
    [ "cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.lifecycleStatus == 'IN_DISPUTE'",
      "cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.totalAmount > 1000" ]
  ]
}
```
A bare string here returns 400 "expecting object at filter". `filter: null` means no filter.

# Common nodes (after the trigger)

Control flow:
- `IfNode` — binary decision. `condition` (full `cel:` expression evaluated inline, e.g. `cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.totalAmount > 1000.0`), `nextIfTrue`, `nextIfFalse`. The legacy `$path.bool` ref form still parses but is deprecated (see the `$`-parser bugs below).
- `BranchNode` — N branches. `branches: [{name, conditions, nextNode}, ...]` (`name` = required non-empty string label; `conditions` = nested OR/AND arrays of full `cel:` expressions, same nesting as the trigger filter), plus `default` (required string slug — `""` when there is no else path, NEVER null) and optional `defaultName`.
- `WaitNode` — delay. `waitMode: {type: "Duration", seconds: 20}`, `nextNode`.
- `FailNode` — explicitly fail. `errorMessage`, no `nextNode`.

Data:
- `CodeNode` — compute values with CEL. `code` (CEL object, `cel:` prefix), `nextNode`.
- `MappingNode` — lookup table. `input`, `mappings`, `default`, `nextNode`.
- `FetchCustomFieldsNode` — get custom fields. Fields are `objectId`, `objectType` (NOT entityId/entityType). Returns a flat dict under `storage.<slug>` keyed by CF name.

Approval:
- `CheckNode` — approval workflow. `objectId`, `objectType`, `reviewers[]`, `passThreshold`, `refuseThreshold`, `nextIfPassed`, `nextIfRefused`. Reviewer types: `User`, `Team`, `BusinessUnit`. `objectType` is a RESTRICTED enum distinct from the trigger entity type — e.g. a `Partnership` trigger uses `objectType: "OrganizationRelationship"`, NOT `"Partnership"`. Call `get_flow_node_catalog` for the exact allowed set.

HTTP / email:
- `HttpNodeV2` — `url`, `method`, `body`, `headers`, `auth`, `nextIfSuccess`, `nextIfFailure`.
- `SendEmailNodeV2` — `recipients[]`, `subject`, `bodyHtml`, `nextNode`.

Business entity nodes (use these — don't rebuild in CodeNode):
- `InvoiceToPurchaseOrderMatchNode` — 3-way matching native. `nextIfMatched` / `nextIfNotMatched`.
- `SetTransactionLifecycleStatusNode` — transitions a transaction document's state. `statusToSet` is a CEL literal like `"'APPROVED'"`.
- `CreateTaskNode` — create a task (e.g. from a classified email). `title` is required.
- `GenAiNode` — call another agent (classification, extraction) mid-flow.
- `ApprovePurchaseRequestNode`, `ApprovePurchaseRequestLineNode`, `ConvertPrToPoNode`, `RefusePurchaseRequestNode`, `CreatePurchaseRequestNode`, `LinkInvoiceAndPurchaseOrderNode`, `AssignTagNode`, `CreateTagNode`, `AssignBusinessUnitsToObjectNode`, `AssignDocumentToObjectNode`.

Call `get_flow_node_catalog` for the full set and exact field shapes — the list above is just the most common.

BU-resolution nodes (for dynamic approval routing):
- `FetchObjectBusinessUnitsNode` — BUs linked to an object — THE node for "requester's BU".
- `FetchUserBusinessUnitsNode`, `FetchBusinessUnitHierarchyNode`, `FetchBusinessUnitNode`, `FetchManagersNode`.

# CEL prefix rules (the parser is NOT unified across nodes)

| Field | Prefix | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `CodeNode.code` | `cel:` (no `$` inside) | `"cel:{ 'foo': entity_trigger_1.invoice.id }"` |
| `IfNode.condition` | `cel:` (full expression inline) | `"cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.totalAmount > 1000.0"` |
| `BranchNode.branches[].conditions` | `cel:` (full expressions inline) | `[["cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.totalAmount > 5000.0"]]` |
| `CheckNode.objectId` | `cel:` | `"cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.id"` |
| `CheckNode.reviewers[].teamId/userId/businessUnitId` | Bare CEL literal `'uuid'` (static) or `cel:node.path` (dynamic) | `"'3f985372-...'"` or `"cel:mapping_4.lvl1"` |
| `HttpNodeV2.url/method/body` | `cel:` | `"cel:'https://api.erp.com'"` |
| `HttpNodeV2.headers` | none — bare JSON object | `{ "Content-Type": "application/json" }` (the map is NOT `cel:`; only individual header *values* may be `cel:`) |
| `SetTransactionLifecycleStatusNode.statusToSet` | Bare CEL literal | `"'APPROVED'"` |
| `CreateTaskNode.title` and other `ApiExpression` fields | `cel:node.path` ref OR bare CEL literal | `"cel:classify.task_title"` or `"'Review email'"` |

**All node-output references use `cel:`.** To reference an upstream node's output anywhere — conditions, `objectId`, reviewer ids, action-node fields, the trigger filter — write a full `cel:` expression (operators, method calls, membership allowed inline), e.g. `cel:code_56.buyer.addressLine1 != null && code_56.buyer.addressLine1 != ''` or `cel:'684ab0a2...' in entity_trigger_1.invoice.parties`. Static ids (reviewer/team UUIDs, status literals) are bare single-quoted CEL literals like `'APPROVED'`. This is the dominant, fully-supported form in production. Use it.

Symptoms: missing `cel:` on a reference field → stored as a literal string instead of an evaluated expression; `$` inside a `cel:` block → "CEL compilation failed, token recognition error at '$'".

# The legacy `$`-prefix reference form is DEPRECATED

Older flows referenced node outputs with a bare `$path` prefix (e.g. `$parse.is_high`, `$entity_trigger_1.invoice.id`) instead of `cel:`. **Do not emit `$`-prefixed references** — they are deprecated. The `$`-prefix parser also has known corruption bugs that deploy as HTTP 204 successes:
- `==` is silently stripped to `=` (assignment, always truthy).
- A trailing `)` is silently dropped from the stored expression.
- Nested `'...'` quotes inside method calls (`replace(' ','')`) truncate the expression.

`cel:`-prefix is IMMUNE to all three. Computing a boolean inside a CodeNode (`cel:`) and routing from a pure `$path.bool` ref still parses, but the `$` ref form is discouraged — prefer a `cel:` condition inline (a CodeNode remains a valid option for sharing/organizing logic, not for correctness):

```json
{ "type": "IfNode", "slug": "if_high", "condition": "cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.totalAmount > 90000.0", "nextIfTrue": "check_directoire", "nextIfFalse": "auto_approve" }
```

# CEL essentials inside `cel:` blocks
- Use `has(x.field)` before accessing nullable paths.
- Operators: `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `&&`, `||`, `!`, ternary `cond ? a : b`.
- Strings: `.contains()`, `.startsWith()`, `.replace(' ','')`, `.upperAscii()`, `.split('-')`.
- Numbers: `double(s)`, `int(s)`, `math.round()`, `math.abs()`, `sumBy(items, 'field')`.
- Arrays: `size(items)`, `items.map(i, i.x)`, `items.filter(i, i.active)`, `items.exists(i, i.x == y)`.
- Membership: `"key" in map`, `"value" in [list]`.

# Minimal end-to-end example
```json
{
  "name": "Approve invoice > 1000",
  "enabled": false,
  "nodes": [
    {
      "type": "EntityTriggerNode",
      "slug": "entity_trigger_1",
      "entity": {"type": "Invoice", "startMode": {"type": "OnEntityCreated"}, "restartMode": {"type": "Manual"}, "currencyConversion": {"type": "Disabled"}, "includeVersionEvents": false},
      "filter": null,
      "nextNode": "if_high"
    },
    {
      "type": "IfNode",
      "slug": "if_high",
      "condition": "cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.totalAmount > 1000.0",
      "nextIfTrue": "approve",
      "nextIfFalse": null
    },
    {
      "type": "CheckNode",
      "slug": "approve",
      "objectId": "cel:entity_trigger_1.invoice.id",
      "objectType": "Invoice",
      "reviewers": [{"type": "Team", "teamId": "'finance-team-uuid'"}],
      "passThreshold": 1,
      "refuseThreshold": 1,
      "nextIfPassed": null,
      "nextIfRefused": null
    }
  ]
}
```

tools.name: update_flow
tools.title: Update flow
tools.description:
Update an existing flow (deploys a new version).

ALWAYS call `get_flow` first to read the current shape — partial updates are not supported; you must send the complete nodes array. Bump `version` by exactly +1 from the current. Forgetting any required field returns 400 with the field path in the error body — read it.

# Required fields on PUT (not all documented in OpenAPI)
- `version`: must be current + 1, else 409 "version already exists".
- `archived`: required even when unchanged (typically `false`).
- `enabled`: required.
- `nodes`: complete array (full replacement, not a patch).
- For `EntityTriggerNode` trigger, the `entity` object REQUIRES `currencyConversion` (use `{"type": "Disabled"}` unless converting to a target currency) — copy it from the GET response verbatim; omitting it 400s "Missing required field at 'nodes[0].entity.currencyConversion'".

# Workflow
1. `get_flow(flow_id, version=N)` — fetch current shape.
2. Mutate the node array as needed; preserve `entity` shape verbatim.
3. `update_flow(flow_id, version=N+1, name, enabled, archived, nodes)` — returns 204.
4. **Verify**: `get_flow(flow_id, version=N+1)` and inspect the stored expressions. Prefer `cel:` for IfNode/BranchNode conditions (immune to the parser bugs below). If you kept any legacy `$`-prefix condition, inspect it character-for-character — the `$`-prefix parser has corruption bugs that deploy as HTTP 204 successes:
   - `==` silently becomes `=` (assignment, always truthy).
   - Trailing `)` silently stripped.
   - Nested `'...'` in `.replace()` / `.split()` truncates the expression at the first inner quote.
   If you see any `==`, `)`, or nested quote in a `$`-prefix condition, rewrite it as a `cel:` inline condition (immune) — or move the logic into a CodeNode (`cel:`) and read a pure `$path.bool` reference.

value.description: A string, number or boolean; a list for `in` / `notIn`; true/false for `null` / `notNull`. Send the value JSON-encoded in this string: true, 42, "some text", {"key": 1}, [1, 2] or null. Text that is not valid JSON is used as is.

conditions.description: Filters, ANDed: [{field, op, value}]. Use them for EVERY criterion the user gave — never answer with a list filtered on only part of the question. Operators: eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, contains / notContains (case-insensitive, text fields only), in / notIn (value is a list), null / notNull (value true/false). Fields: id, number, documentType (INVOICE, CREDIT_NOTE, DEBIT_NOTE, PURCHASE_ORDER, SALES_ORDER, QUOTE, PURCHASE_REQUEST, GOODS_RECEIPT, EXPENSE), source (NETWORK, EMAIL, UPLOAD, UPLOAD_LINK, API, IMPORT, SYNC, EMBEDDED_FILE, OCR, INTERNAL_SERVICE, FLOWIE, UNKNOWN), externalDocumentId, originalInvoiceId, purchaseOrderId; dates issuedAt, dueDate and timestamps createdAt, updatedAt (ISO date, or today, now, yesterday, tomorrow, start_of_month, start_of_previous_month, start_of_year, start_of_previous_year; a date on a timestamp means midnight, so use lt the next day for 'up to and including'); amounts totalAmountExclTax, totalAmountInclTax, totalTax (numbers), currency; party ids sellerId (seller side), payerId / buyerId (buyer side); party names sellerName, payerName, buyerName; people createdBy.id, createdBy.name, assignee.id, assignee.name; lifecycleStatus (the organization's own status labels, see list_lifecycles); template.id, template.name; tagIds and businessUnitIds (eq, ne, in, notIn only; a business unit includes its descendants); taxAuthorityStatusCode, taxAuthorityStatusLabel; hasDuplicates (true/false); transactionId, paymentReferenceNumber, paymentInstructions, paymentTermsId, notes, conditions, statusReason.

value.description: A string, number or boolean; a list for `in` / `notIn`; true/false for `null` / `notNull`. Send the value JSON-encoded in this string: true, 42, "some text", {"key": 1}, [1, 2] or null. Text that is not valid JSON is used as is.

any_of.description: OR between groups: at least one group must match, each group's conditions ANDed, e.g. [[{field: sellerName, op: contains, value: acme}], [{field: payerName, op: contains, value: acme}]] for Acme on either side. Combined with `conditions` by AND.

sort.description: <field>:asc or <field>:desc (default createdAt:desc). Fields: createdAt, updatedAt, issuedAt, dueDate, number, totalAmountInclTax, sellerName, buyerName, payerName, createdBy, assignee, createdByUserId, assigneeUserId, source, taxAuthorityStatusCode, lifecycleStatus.

query.description: Free-text search, as in the app's search box (document types).

ids.description: Export exactly these rows (e.g. the ids a search returned).

view.description: Document types: 'buyer' = documents the organization pays (received / purchases), 'supplier' = documents it issued (sales), 'all' (default) = both.

columns.description: Keep only these columns, in this order (column keys of the export).

template.description: A saved export template (name or id from list_export_templates): its columns, labels and options. For transaction types, partners, budgets and form-submissions.

include.description: Extra columns. Orders, purchase requests, quotes, sales orders, receipts, delivery notes, proformas, transactions: lines (one row per line item), approvals, deep_link (link to the document in the app), computed, supplier_registration, budget_metrics, business_unit_hierarchy, requester, linked_documents. enrichment.description: Resolve ids to names (default true); false is faster.

language.description: Language of column headers and labels, e.g. 'fr' or 'en' (default: the user's).

filters.description: Other query parameters of the list being exported, passed as-is — for non-document exports (tasks, payments, budgets, partners: e.g. {"type": "supplier"}). Document exports use `conditions`.

tools.name: get_rule
tools.title: Get rule
tools.description: Get one rule with full detail (targets, expression / value, severity / attribute, timestamps).

organization_id.description: Read this organization instead of the current one. Must be the current organization or one of its sub-organizations — call list_sub_organizations to get the ids. Omit it for the current organization.

tools.name: create_constraint_rule
tools.title: Create constraint rule
tools.description: Create a Constraint rule — validates an entity. If `expression` evaluates to false at evaluation time, the rule produces a finding of `severity`. Use to enforce business rules (e.g. 'invoice total must be > 0', 'PO must have at least one line item').

expression.description: CEL boolean expression — must evaluate true for the rule to pass.

type.description: Entity type this rule applies to.

id.description: Optional: scope to one specific entity ID. Omit to apply to ALL of `type`.

targets.description: Entity types (and optionally specific IDs) this rule applies to.

field.description: Optional: which field the rule is about (used for UI highlighting).

error_message.description: Message shown to the user when the rule fails.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: create_derivation_rule
tools.title: Create derivation rule
tools.description: Create a Derivation rule — auto-derives a UI attribute of `field` (defaultValue, hidden, maxLength, options, pattern, placeholder, readOnly). When `condition` is omitted the derivation always applies; when present, the derivation only applies when the CEL `condition` evaluates true. Use to dynamically adjust form fields (e.g. 'hide tax field when supplier country is non-EU').

field.description: Name of the field to derive.

attribute.description: Which attribute of the field to set.

value.description: Value to assign. Type depends on attribute (boolean for hidden/readOnly, integer for maxLength, string for placeholder/pattern, etc.). Send the value JSON-encoded in this string: true, 42, "some text", {"key": 1}, [1, 2] or null. Text that is not valid JSON is used as is.

type.description: Entity type this rule applies to.

id.description: Optional: scope to one specific entity ID. Omit to apply to ALL of `type`.

targets.description: Entity types (and optionally IDs) this rule applies to.

condition.description: Optional CEL expression — derivation only applies when true.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: update_rule
tools.title: Update rule
tools.description: Patch a rule. Send only the fields you want to change. The shape accepts the union of Constraint and Derivation fields — the server applies whichever apply to this rule's kind.

type.description: Entity type this rule applies to.

id.description: Optional: scope to one specific entity ID. Omit to apply to ALL of `type`.

value.description: Derivation-only. Send the value JSON-encoded in this string: true, 42, "some text", {"key": 1}, [1, 2] or null. Text that is not valid JSON is used as is.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: delete_rule
tools.title: Delete rule

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: evaluate_rules
tools.title: Evaluate rules
tools.description:
Evaluate rules against arbitrary data and get the outcome — constraint findings (errors/warnings/info) and any derivations applied. Pass `data` as the entity payload (JSON dict). Three modes:
  • `rule_id` only — evaluate that single rule against `data`.
  • `target` (type + optional id) only — evaluate ALL matching rules.
  • `rule_ids` array — evaluate only those rules (uses v2 batch endpoint).
Use this to test a rule before enabling it (run against a known-good and a known-bad payload), or to validate an entity ad-hoc before persisting.

data.description: The entity payload to evaluate against.

rule_id.description: Evaluate a single rule by ID. Mutually exclusive with rule_ids/target.

target.description: Used when evaluating all matching rules. Provide entity type and optionally id.

data_type.description: When using rule_id mode, the entity type of `data`.

organization_id.description: Read this organization instead of the current one. Must be the current organization or one of its sub-organizations — call list_sub_organizations to get the ids. Omit it for the current organization.

tools.name: create_catalog
tools.title: Create catalog
tools.description: Create a new, empty product catalog in the organization. A catalog groups products either FOR_SALE (things the organization sells) or FOR_PURCHASE (things it buys); add products afterwards with create_product or bulk_import_products. It changes no existing catalog or product, and only members of the organization can see it: sharing a catalog with another organization is done in the Flowie app, not here. Use this when the organization has no catalog yet or wants to separate product lines.

type.description: Whether this catalog holds products the org sells or buys

access_type.description: Visibility inside the organization, as the Flowie app labels it. Either way the catalog stays within the organization. Default: PRIVATE.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: create_product
tools.title: Create product
tools.description: Create a single product and add it to a catalog. Prices/variants are not set by this tool — the founder configures them separately. Use bulk_import_products instead when adding more than ~5 items at once.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: update_product
tools.title: Update product
tools.description: Update an existing product. Both `name` (label) and `status` are required by the product-catalog service; pass the current values for fields you don't want to change. Use status=DISCONTINUED to deactivate.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: bulk_import_products
tools.title: Bulk import products
tools.description: Create multiple products and add each to the same catalog. Useful during onboarding when the founder has a list of items to add (typically 10-200). Returns a per-row result so partial failures don't block the whole import. Prices/variants are not set — configure them separately.

products.description: List of product objects to create

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.

tools.name: get_navigation_visibility
tools.title: Get navigation visibility
tools.description: Read which navigation items the organization's members see: the organization defaults (items hidden for everyone unless a member shows them again from 'Customize sidebar') and each role's restrictions (items that role can never see). Also returns every item key with its label, which is what set_navigation_visibility takes.

organization_id.description: Read this organization instead of the current one. Must be the current organization or one of its sub-organizations — call list_sub_organizations to get the ids. Omit it for the current organization.

tools.name: set_navigation_visibility
tools.title: Set navigation visibility
tools.description: Hide or show navigation items, as on the app's Navigation visibility settings page. scope='organization' changes the defaults for every member (they can still show a hidden item again for themselves). scope='role' restricts a role: its members cannot see the item at all, and settings sections or pages can be restricted too ('settings-nav-all' closes the whole settings area). Only the keys listed in hide/show change; everything else is kept. Items flagged hidden_by_product_default cannot be shown for a whole organization; each member shows them from 'Customize sidebar'. Call get_navigation_visibility first for the keys and the role ids.

scope.description: 'organization' for everyone's defaults, 'role' for one role's restrictions.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in. Defaults to the client's X-Flowie-Organization-Id header, else the user's first organization. See list_my_organizations.
